evidence.quotedText: Administrator instructs Alaio to process Personal Data only in accordance with applicable law: (a) to provide the Processor Services and any related technical support; (b) as further specified via Administrator´s use of the Processor Services (including in the settings and other functionality of the Processor Services) and any related technical support; (c) as documented in this Data Processing Agreement; and (d) as further documented in any other written instructions given by Administrator and acknowledged by Bitrix24 as constituting instructions for purposes of this Data Processing Agreement.

findings.claim: The quote expressly confirms that all persons authorized to process personal data are committed to contractual or statutory confidentiality.

findings.establishedBy: Alaio ensures that all persons authorized to process personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.

findings.claim: Expressly obligates implementation of technical, physical, and organisational measures and details specific categories including ongoing confidentiality, availability, resilience, timely restoration, and testing of effectiveness.

evidence.quotedText: Alaio will implement and maintain technical, physical and organisational measures to protect confidentiality and integrity of Personal Data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure or access as described in the Appendix 2 to this DPA (the “Security Measures”). findings.establishedBy: Establishes that the processor must implement and maintain technical, physical, and organisational security measures covering confidentiality, resilience, restoration, and regular testing.

findings.claim: States that Alaio will assist Administrator in responding to data subjects' requests to exercise their rights under Chapter III GDPR by providing service functionality.

findings.establishedBy: Establishes that the processor (Alaio) will assist the controller in fulfilling obligations to respond to data subject rights requests under Chapter III GDPR by providing the functionality of the Processor Services.

findings.claim: requires advance notification of new subprocessors and explicitly grants the administrator the right to object in writing.

evidence.quotedText: When any new Sub-processor is engaged during the Term, and if the GDPR applies to the processing of Personal Data, Alaio will, at least 10 days before the new Sub-processor processes any Personal Data, inform Administrator of the engagement (including the name and location of the relevant sub-processor and the activities it will perform) by sending an email to the Notification Email Address. Administrator may object to any new Sub-processor by notifying Alaio promptly in writing within five (5) business days after receipt of Alaio notice.

findings.remediation: Extend the advance notification and objection mechanism to all processing under the DPA regardless of GDPR applicability.
findings.establishedBy: Establishes a general authorization framework with prior notice and an explicit right for the controller/administrator to object to new sub-processors under the GDPR.
findings.gapDescription: Applies specifically when the GDPR applies to the processing of personal data, rather than being an unconditional requirement across all jurisdictions/processing.
findings.structuralNote: This clause represents the general authorization mechanism when read in conjunction with the initial authorization in clause 7.1.

findings.claim: Explicitly commits the processor to assist the controller with its security and breach obligations under Articles 32-34.

evidence.quotedText: Alaio will assist in ensuring compliance with any obligations of Administrator in respect of security of personal data and personal data breaches, including (if applicable) Administrator’s obligations pursuant to Articles 32 to 34 (inclusive) of the GDPR, by: (a) implementing and maintaining the Security Measures in accordance with the Appendix 2 to this DPA;

findings.remediation: Combine with clause 10 to establish assistance across all Articles 32-36.
findings.establishedBy: Establishes that the processor assists the controller with security of processing and personal data breach obligations (Articles 32-34).
findings.gapDescription: Does not cover DPIA and prior consultation obligations under Articles 35-36 (which are covered in clause 10 / S30).
findings.structuralNote: Security/breach assistance and DPIA assistance are split across separate clauses in the DPA.

findings.claim: Clause 2.5 mandates deletion of all Personal Data including existing copies on term expiry unless applicable law requires storage, satisfying the core end-of-service processing mandate but omitting the return choice option.

evidence.quotedText: On expiry of the Term, Administrator instructs Alaio to delete all Personal Data (including existing copies) from Bitrix24 systems in accordance with applicable law. Alaio will comply with this instruction as soon as reasonably practicable and within a maximum period of 90 days, unless any applicable law requires storage.

findings.remediation: Add express terms providing the Administrator with the option to choose between the return or deletion of personal data upon term expiry.
findings.establishedBy: The passage establishes an automatic instruction upon term expiry to delete all Personal Data (including existing copies) subject to legal storage exceptions.
findings.gapDescription: The passage mandates deletion only and does not provide an alternative option for the controller (Administrator) to elect the return of personal data.

findings.claim: The clause explicitly obligates Alaio to make available compliance information to the Administrator or its auditor and allows for on-site inspections.

evidence.quotedText: Alaio shall make available to User that is not a competitor of Alaio (or Administrator´s independent, third-party auditor that is not a competitor of Bitrix24) information regarding Alaio compliance with the obligations set forth in this DPA and the security measures as described in the Appendix 2 to this DPA. Administrator may contact Alaio to request an on-site inspection of the architecture, systems and procedures relevant to the protection of Personal Data at locations where Personal Data is stored.

findings.establishedBy: Establishes that the processor makes information available to demonstrate compliance and permits on-site audits/inspections by the controller or its auditor.
findings.structuralNote: Imposes a condition that the auditor/User cannot be a competitor.

findings.claim: Explicitly requires imposing Article 28(3) data protection obligations on the Sub-processor and entering into a written agreement containing obligations not less protective than those in the DPA.

evidence.quotedText: (ii) if the GDPR applies to the processing of Personal Data, the data protection obligations set out in Article 28(3) of the GDPR are imposed on the Sub-processor; (b) Alaio have entered into a written agreement with each Sub-processor containing data protection obligations not less protective than those in this DPA with respect to the protection of Personal Data to the extent applicable to the nature of the Services provided by such Sub-processor;

findings.establishedBy: Alaio must ensure by written contract that Article 28(3) obligations are imposed on the Sub-processor and that data protection obligations are not less protective than those in the DPA.
findings.structuralNote: Clause 7.2 combines standard contract terms, Article 28(3) references, and subprocessor liability in a single section.

Analysis target:
Treat the uploaded DPA as the target document. Apply the active GDPR Article 28 compliance rule package as the governing standard.

Scope:
Assess whether the agreement adequately specifies:

The subject matter of processing.
The duration of processing.
The nature and purpose of processing.
The categories of personal data.
The categories of data subjects.
The controller’s relevant rights and obligations.

Evidence standard:
For every requirement, identify the exact clause or provision supporting the conclusion. Include the clause number and a complete, relevant quotation. Do not treat definitions, unrelated provisions, or generic compliance statements as proof of a specific obligation.

Adequacy rules:
Distinguish between:

Present and adequate
Partially covered
Missing
Dependent on referenced material
Not applicable

Mark a requirement “Present and adequate” only when the available agreement contains sufficient operative language to satisfy that requirement.

Missing-material treatment:
If a requirement may be covered by a referenced annex, schedule, SOW, policy, or external document that was not uploaded, do not classify it as definitively missing or satisfied. Mark it as “Dependent on referenced material” and identify the exact missing document.

Do not invent clauses, infer unseen language, or rely on general assumptions about standard DPAs.

Provide:

A concise overall conclusion.
A requirement matrix with columns:
   Requirement | Status | Clause and evidence | Analysis | Recommended action
A separate list of material gaps.
A list of missing referenced documents.
A prioritized remediation summary.
